(1) the transcriptional regulator Clrc of Sinorhizo- bium meliloti controls secondary infection of Medica- gosativalba roots, (2) Clrc activates expression of a so- far unknown polysaccharidic compound, (3) Clrc activates the synthesis of succinoglycane, (4) Clrc negatively controls the expression of motility and chemosensory genes, (5) Clrc activates three genes of unknown

the cAMP-dependent transcription factor Clr of S. melioti regulates the synthesis of c-di-GMP and cAMP-dependent succingoglycan as part of a regulatory network that controls secondary infection on Medicago sativa.

the transcriptional regulator ClrcAMP of Sinorhazobium melilotis controls the overall number of secondary infection events of M. sativa roots by a mechanism that requires the ClrcAMP target genes smc02178 (symbiotic), smc02177 (symbiotic) and smb20495 (symbiotic and ex planta).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of novel genes involved in the symbiotic interaction of Medicago roots with Sinorhizobia.
the control of secondary symbiotic infection of Medicago truncatula and Medicago sativa roots by Sinorhizobia.
the control of symbiotic infection in legumes by Sinorhizobia and more specifically with the role of a cAMP-dependent transcription factor in this process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the cAMP-dependent regulator Clr of S. melilioti controls the overall number of secondary infection events on M. satvia roots by a mechanism requiring smc 02178 and smb 20495, two genes of unknown function that are activated by a plant signal.

the Clr-activated gene smc02177 is a positive modulator of the control of secondary infections by S. melilotis on M. sativae, whereas the Clr- activated genes smb20495 and the so far uncharacterized gene smc02178 are negative modulators of the control of this process.
Clr controls the synthesis of a cAMP-dependent polysaccharide that is required for secondary infection.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Clr transcriptional activator of S. melilothi controls the number of infection events of Medicago roots through the regulation of a complex network of genes, including smc02177/smc02178, smb20395, and other Clr-activated and Clr-repressed genes.
the cAMP-dependent transcription regulator Clr of S. melilioti is a key player for the control of root secondary infection by the rhizobium.
Clr controls secondary infection of Med. sativa by a two-step process.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Clr regulon is not limited to the control of the overall number of root infection sites, but includes a number of genes involved in symbiotic root infection and possibly in the control of the symbiotic phenotype of the bacterium.
Clr controls the expression of a large set of genes, including a number of genes of unknown function.
